steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Greek philosophy began with questioning the nature of the universe; early philosophers sought natural rather than divine explanations

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The Sophists were professional teachers who travelled offering instruction in rhetoric and persuasion for pay; they claimed to make the weaker argument appear stronger

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Socrates (469-399 BC) challenged assumptions through questioning (the Socratic method/dialectic); he sought truth rather than persuasion

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Socrates was tried and executed (399 BC) for impiety and corrupting the youth; his trial illustrates the tension between free thought and Athenian democracy

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: How did Socrates differ from the Sophists? | Q: What was the Socratic method? | Q: Why was Socrates put on trial?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Socrates sought truth through questioning (dialectic) and did not charge fees. The Sophists taught rhetoric and persuasion for pay, claiming to make the weaker argument appear stronger. steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Socrates vs Sophists: truth vs persuasion, free vs paid Socratic method = questions that expose contradictions Trial of Socrates: impiety + corrupting youth; really about politics Plato's dialogues are our main source for Socrates
